3.2.5 One Dimensional and Two Dimensional Models

The scheme as so far described allows for infiltration and vertical
flow in heterogeneous soils with pore pressure estimations made according
to equation 3.29 for all locations within perched water tables (see table
3.2).

_ To generalise this model to two dimensions requires further approxi-
mations. In coupling several one dimensional models (Figure 3.5) together
+o form a two dimensional mcdel (Figure 3.2b) it is convenient to employ the
Dupuit-Forchheimer assumptions. These assumptions state that in a system of
gravity flow toward a shallow sink (i.e. the toe of the slope) all the
groundwater flow is horizontal, and that the velocity at each point is
proportional to the slope of the water table but independent of depth.
Hillel (1977) observes that these assumptions are not correct in the strict
sense but they provide feasible soluticns in a very simple form. Thus if
the effective gradient is taken to be. equal to the slope of the water table
